title: deadline-aware decode preemption and KV warmup scheduler with micro-slice packing
author: Maya Singh
commits: 9c1f4b2: introduce deadline-aware priority field on requests
a72d0f8: implement micro-slice packing algorithm and packing tests
b8e33a1: add KV warmup manager and async priming hooks
f3b20d7: integrate preemptible_dispatch with scheduling and metrics
d4a7cfe: add feature flag and config profile; update docs and changelog
description:
Context & motivation: High P99 decode tail latency on mixed workloads comes from long-running decodes blocking short, latency-sensitive requests when CPU/GPU kernels are monopolized by large batches. Existing continuous-batching + prefill strategies reduce throughput cost but struggle when a small high-priority request arrives mid-prefill window. This PR introduces a deadline-aware scheduler that enables lightweight decode preemption combined with proactive KV cache warmup (priming) and a micro-slice packing layer that coalesces tiny decode slices to retain throughput.

Design summary: We add three cooperating components: (1) deadline_scheduler - assigns soft deadlines to incoming requests and can preempt pending decode slices when a higher-deadline candidate arrives; (2) micro_slice_packer - splits large decode work into micro-slices (configurable slice size) and packs small latency-sensitive slices opportunistically to avoid throughput loss; (3) kvcache warmup_manager - issues async KV priming requests for expected future continuations for requests that are likely to be preempted or for high-hit-rate prefixes. The scheduler uses a simple EDF-inspired heuristic with a preemption budget per worker to avoid thrashing. The warmup manager is conservative by default (configurable aggressiveness) and integrates with existing KV eviction/soft-evict signals.

Implementation notes: The scheduler lives in src/runtime/scheduler/deadline_scheduler.rs and exposes hooks into dispatcher (preemptible_dispatch.rs). Preemption is cooperative: decode kernels must check a preemption token at kernel slice boundaries; we use a fast atomic flag and a small handshake to migrate half-completed KV cache slots. Micro-slice packing is implemented as an intermediate layer before kernel submission; the code ensures token cache coherency by carrying a short-lived KV priming context with each packed slice. All new components are behind runtime feature flags (runtime.features.decode_preemption, runtime.features.kv_warmup) and can be toggled per model or route in configs/profiles/deadline_defaults.yaml.

Benchmarks & results: CI microbenchmarks and a patched perf lab run show: median latency change: -3% (unchanged for bulk workloads), p95: -12% for mixed traffic (10% small latency-sensitive requests), p99: -28% on a 80/20 small/large mix using slice_size=64 tokens and preemption_budget=3. Throughput drop observed in heavy bulk-only synthetic runs is <2% when micro-slice packing is enabled. KV warmup reduced cold-KV miss rate for preempted continuations from 42% to 9% in our instrumented traces.

Testing and rollout: Unit tests cover scheduler invariants, preemption handshake correctness, and KV warmup backoff. Integration tests exercise multi-request interleaving and ensure no state leakage between slices. Benchmarks/bench_decode_preemption.py reproduces perf numbers. Rollout strategy: enable feature flag in staging for 2 weeks with conservative defaults (slice_size=64, preemption_budget=1, kv_warmup=low); ramp to canary (5%) then to 50% with observability dashboards (decode latency heatmaps, kvcache hit/miss per route) added in this PR.

Risks and mitigations: Primary risk is preemption-induced cache churn hurting throughput. Mitigations: preemption budget, conservative default warmup policy, and automatic rollback if aggregate throughput drops by >5% in a rolling window. Another risk is kernel compatibility: we added a lightweight kernel callback to check preemption token — legacy kernels fall back to non-preemptible path.

Related: Linear ENG-4321 (deadline scheduling proto), ENG-4389 (KV warmup design). Sup ticket SUP-7823 reported customer incidents where short requests suffered huge tail latency.

Checklist: [x] design doc updated (docs/architecture/decode-preemption.md) [x] unit/integration tests [x] perf benchmarks added [x] feature flags + config profile [x] rollout/monitoring notes
review_conversation: Ethan Caldwell (reviewer) on 2024-10-03: Great direction. Can you explain why we chose cooperative preemption vs immediate kernel termination? Concerned about GPU kernel teardown overhead.

Maya Singh (author) on 2024-10-03: Answered: cooperative avoids heavy teardown; we split kernels into micro-slices and check a preempt flag at slice boundaries. Empirical overhead of a slice boundary check is <0.2% (measured).

Luca Moretti (reviewer) on 2024-10-04: Suggestion: add a safeguard that disables preemption on low-util hosts to avoid unnecessary packing overhead. Also request metrics for preemption counts per worker.

Maya Singh (author) on 2024-10-05: Implemented an API to read host utilization and added preemption gating; added metrics decode.preemptions.total and decode.preemptions.per_worker. Updated tests to cover gating behavior.
Zoe Chen (reviewer) on 2024-10-06: Please make warmup aggressiveness configurable per-model and ensure it respects privacy flags for private deployments.
Maya Singh (author) on 2024-10-07: Done - config supports per-model overrides and warmup is disabled automatically for models/routes marked privacy.sensitive. Added docs note.
Ethan Caldwell (reviewer) on 2024-10-09: CI flake on bench job; re-ran and green. Approving pending changelog entry.
Maya Singh (author) on 2024-10-10: Added changelog entry and a short migration note in docs. Marking ready to merge.
release_notes: Introduce deadline-aware decode preemption and KV warmup scheduler. Improves P99 decode latency on mixed workloads by allowing short high-priority requests to preempt long-running decodes while maintaining throughput via micro-slice packing. Feature gated behind runtime.features.decode_preemption and runtime.features.kv_warmup.
